newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lernout buys German firm for $14.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Lernout buys German firm for $14.7 mln.

text.p: Belgian Nasdaq-listed high technology firm Lernout & Hauspie Speech Products NV said on Wednesday it had acquired German machine translation company Gesellschaft fuer Multilinguale System GmbH (GMS) for $14.7 million in cash and new shares.

"L&H acquired GMS for approximately $14.7 million, $10.7 million of which is in cash and $4 million in newly issued shares of L&H common stock. The acquisition is expected to be non-dilutive for 1997 and is expected to contribute to the company's earnings thereafter," L&H said in a statement.
The GMS acquisition would "strongly increase" L&H's presence in the translation market, accelerating its efforts to bring to market multi-lingual Internet translation services, it said.
L&H said it hopes to offer a pilot of the Internet service before the end of 1997 for the Spanish/English and German/English language pairs.
Commercial services should roll out from the beginning of 1998, with other language pairs being added during that year.
